reuse.why: Copies the `COALESCE(JSON_EXTRACT(template_settings,'$.source'),'notes') <> 'ui'` idiom from statements.ts into four queries and adds a separate JS `template_source === 'ui'` check, instead of introducing one shared 'should fill this category' predicate or query that all month-wide actions use.

duplication.why: The template exclusion is written five times (four SQL WHERE clauses and one JS check in copyPreviousMonth), and setZero's query is rewritten into a fourth copy of the hidden/group-hidden filtering query shared by the average actions.

placement.why: The rule stays in budget/actions.ts where the month-wide actions live, but it is split between SQL WHERE clauses and an in-loop JS check rather than living in one function in that module.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions, a test and the necessary query/type changes are touched.

maintainability.why: Changing what counts as 'left untouched' now means editing five places in two languages (SQL and TS) that must stay consistent; the test covers only set3MonthAvg.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The tree has no shared fill predicate in actions.ts to go around; the change follows the existing per-action filtering pattern instead of introducing one

disguised_duplication.where: The same exclusion rule is expressed once as a JS comparison on a selected `template_source` column (copyPreviousMonth/getBudgetData) and four times as a SQL COALESCE filter (setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg), so it looks different but is the same logic

one_place.where: The rule is applied separately in copyPreviousMonth (JS check), setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg (SQL clauses) in server/budget/actions.ts, with no shared definition
